title: Advanced Functions: Defaults, *args, **kwargs, Docstrings
objectives: Define functions with default parameter values

content.title: Default Parameter Values
content.explanation: Parameters can have default values, making them optional. Defaults are evaluated once at function definition time, not at each call.
key_points: Required params must come before defaults

content.title: Default Parameters
content.explanation: Defaults allow flexible calling. Keyword args let you skip middle defaults.

content.title: Mutable Default Argument Pitfall
content.explanation: Mutable defaults (lists, dicts) are shared across all calls because they are evaluated once at definition. This causes unexpected behavior. Use None as sentinel instead.
key_points: All calls share the SAME list
None is immutable and safe as default

content.title: Mutable Default Bug and Fix
content.code:
# BUGGY
def add_item_buggy(item, items=[]):
    items.append(item)
    return items

content.explanation: The buggy version accumulates across calls. The fixed version creates new list each call.

content.title: *args and **kwargs
content.explanation: *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple. **kwargs collects extra keyword arguments into a dict. Enables flexible function signatures.

content.title: *args and **kwargs Examples
content.code:

# name: Alice
# age: 30
flexible(1, 2, 3, 4, x=10, y=20)
# a=1, b=2, args=(3,4), kwargs={x:10, y:20}
content.explanation: *args packs positional, **kwargs packs keyword. Unpack with * and ** when calling.

content.title: Docstrings
content.explanation: Docstrings document functions. Place as first statement in function. Access via __doc__ or help(). Use Google or NumPy style for consistency.
key_points: Tools like Sphinx extract for documentation

content.title: Google-Style Docstring
content.explanation: Structured docstring with Args, Returns, Raises sections. Machine-readable.

Mutable Default Bug
exercises.description: Demonstrate the mutable default bug and fix it. Create a function that adds to a list, show the bug, then fix with None.
exercises.solution:
# Buggy
def add_buggy(x, lst=[]):
    lst.append(x)
    return lst

print(add_buggy(1))  # [1]
print(add_buggy(2))  # [1, 2] - BUG!

# Fixed
def add_fixed(x, lst=None):
    if lst is None:
        lst = []
    lst.append(x)
    return lst

print(add_fixed(1))  # [1]
print(add_fixed(2))  # [2] - Fixed!
hints: Show bug first, then None sentinel fix

quiz.question: Why is def func(items=[]) dangerous?
options: All calls share the same list object
quiz.correct_answer: All calls share the same list object
quiz.explanation: The default list is created once at definition time. All calls without argument share that same list.
